name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
description: Adversaries send malicious links to targets via email or messaging to induce them to visit a malicious website designed for credential harvesting or malware delivery.
mitigation: Deploy perimeter DNS filtering, enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), and analyze URL structure for lexical anomalies.

name: Acquire Infrastructure: Domains
description: Adversaries register domains with disposable registrars, often maintaining newly registered domains (<30 days old) that mimic legitimate brands or services to bypass legacy domain reputation filters.
mitigation: Flag or restrict inbound connections from domains registered within the last 30 to 60 days; inspect registrar history.

name: Dynamic Resolution: Domain Generation Algorithms (DGA)
description: Adversaries use Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) to dynamically generate hundreds of pseudo-random domain names to establish resilient command and control infrastructure.
mitigation: Implement information-theoretic entropy detection on hostnames and sinkhole high-entropy query patterns.

name: Compromise Infrastructure: DNS / Email Spoofing
description: Adversaries exploit domains lacking SPF (Sender Policy Framework) and DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication) to forge email headers and impersonate legitimate domain owners without detection.
mitigation: Enforce strict SPF (v=spf1 -all) and DMARC policies (p=reject); verify DNS authentication before trusting outbound or inbound messages.

name: Obtain Capabilities: Digital Certificates
description: Adversaries acquire invalid or short-lived TLS/SSL certificates or rely on unencrypted HTTP channels to avoid inspection or present deceptive green padlock trust indicators to victims.
mitigation: Enforce strict TLS certificate validation, inspect certificate transparency logs, and mandate HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security).

name: Defense Evasion: Adversarial URL Smuggling & Domain Framing
description: Adversaries concatenate benign or innocent domain names (lures) with active malicious payloads (e.g. victim.comhttp://malicious-c2.xyz or user@evil.com) to evade reputation filters, bypass automated score gates, and cause denial-of-service/defamation against innocent domain owners by attempting to blacklist innocent domains on public blocklists.
mitigation: Deploy multi-protocol scheme delimiter isolation, disarm framing lures, and scan active payload endpoints independently without attributing threat to prefix hosts.
